newsitem.title: UK: N. Sea crude dormant as buyers wait for price fall.
newsitem.headline: N. Sea crude dormant as buyers wait for price fall.

text.p: North Sea crude markets were dormant in early talk on Friday with sellers under pressure to let differentials slide, traders said.
Cash markets were slightly weaker and little business was expected, with IPE Brent trading barely changed at the $18.20 level reached after Thursday's sharp fall.
The U.S. Independence Day holiday and a trade stalemate meant most players would be doing paperwork or lunch.
"We need someone to make the first move (on North Sea crudes) but I'm not sure we'll see it today," said one trader. "Some of the sellers will have to accept lower numbers."
With most of July North Sea crude requirements covered, buyers were waiting for clarification on the timing of Iraqi of exports and the pressure of poor refinery margins to ease.
"The talks right now are for late July and early August and witht the uncertainty over Iraq and on margins buyers just wonder why they should do anything now," said one broker.
He pointed to a cross-month Ekofisk traded on Thursday at dated Brent -16 cents as evidence of weaker differentials ahead.
Wet Brent was pegged at five cents below August though nothing was heard discussed. Three cargoes were turning wet from the chains on Friday, dated July 19-21, 20-22 and 21-23.
Intermonth spreads were slightly softer, though Jul/Aug was talked steady at +20/+30, while Aug/Sept and Sept/Oct were a cent or so down at -12/-10 cents and -15/10 cents.
Short-term swaps drifted down overnight with next week at -1/+1 cent against August and the following week (July 14-18) pegged at 25 cents below September.
